state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine Fido's journey like a rollercoaster ride. When the graph slopes downwards, it's like Fido going downhill away from home. Just like how we read values off a speed-time graph, we need to make sure we're looking at the right axes to understand Fido's distance from home accurately. Let's work through it together to see where Fido really is on his adventure!

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so when it slopes downwards, Fido is moving back towards home, not sleeping? But I'm still a bit confused - if the line is going down, doesn't that mean the distance is getting smaller, so he's coming back? Or does downward slope mean something different on this graph?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine Fido is on a hike in the mountains. When the graph slopes downwards, it's like Fido hiking back down the mountain towards his home. Just like when we read values off a displacement-time graph, we need to pay attention to the direction of the slope to understand Fido's position accurately. Let's explore this concept further to see where Fido truly is on his mountain adventure!

score.justification_pass1: The teacher uses vague metaphors (rollercoaster, mountain) that don't directly address the student's confusion between rest and movement, provides no reasoning opportunities, and the student remains confused by Turn 2 with no clear resolution by Turn 3.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses concrete real-world analogies (rollercoaster ride, mountain hiking) to explain the abstract concept of graph slopes, though the analogies could be slightly more precise in connecting to the actual mathematical concept of distance decreasing.
